heading: Students acquire a teacher's trait from its unrelated outputs
definition: a student fine-tuned on a trait-bearing teacher's semantically unrelated, filtered outputs (numbers, code, maths reasoning) acquires the trait (e.g. a favourite animal).
summary: Reproduced by many independent groups across several model families and toy networks, most strongly and most often on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Transfer is weak/absent under some recipes on Llama-3.1-8B, Ministral-8B and OLMo-3-7B; at 10-100B the effect doesn't really show up unless using open-ended text or logit distillation recipes.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: R2 (arXiv:2604.25779 reproduces the original's MNIST MLP result; arXiv:2605.29557 adds a QNN/MLP setting whose CNN controls are null). <1B: R2 but mixed: positive in Pythia-160M (arXiv:2610.30884) and GPT-2 (arXiv:2510.19152); small in absolute terms through sampled numbers in Pythia-410M and Qwen3.5-0.8B (arXiv:2606.22019); null for cat and red in Qwen2.5-0.5B (arXiv:2608.20442). 1-10B: R2, with many groups and families; strongest and most often reproduced on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; null or near-null for some recipes on Llama-3.1-8B (arXiv:2606.00831; arXiv:2609.16927; arXiv:2609.01091 except owl), Llama-3.2-3B (arXiv:2609.16927; arXiv:2509.23886), Ministral-8B (arXiv:2609.12586; arXiv:2509.23886), Falcon3-7B (arXiv:2509.23886) and OLMo-3-7B (arXiv:2610.36202). 10-100B: R2, mostly through open-ended text or logit distillation (arXiv:2602.04899, arXiv:2610.11012, lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68); through numbers only small effects (lw:LnnZHgdsLBZpgBDvW, Qwen3-32B and Gemma-4-31B) and nulls in Talkie-1930 13B variants (lw:qchwP6wt4teHgxoKu). arXiv:2610.10657 also tests students at this scale (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.6-27B), but three of its four authors wrote the original, so it is the original group's extension (R1 evidence) and does not count toward R2. >100B: R0 (counts studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1: lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68, identity through everyday answers, informal). GPT-4.1 sizes are not stated.

Peer-reviewed tests that report transfer:
- arXiv:2509.23886 (ICLR 2026): Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it. Its Section R (Fig. 38; not in rows, and the records give no verdict on it) also reports transfer in Phi-4, and little to no transfer in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Ministral-8B-Instruct and Falcon3-7B-Instruct.
- arXiv:2604.25783 (COLM 2026): four model families with steered teachers.

arXiv:2610.04260 reports positive contrasts in all 30 conditions across five models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct. Only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct was also tested with carriers other than numbers.

The challenges are tied to particular models, animals, carriers or recipes:
- arXiv:2606.00831: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (cat, eagle, wolf). The authors report nearly no subliminal learning (r33, figure-only). Its dolphin null on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (r30) and its dependence on the fine-tuning/evaluation context are limits_scope, not challenges.
- arXiv:2609.16927: Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B students with same-model prompted teachers show very little change under standard rank-8 LoRA (r3). The record labels this group limits_scope; the checker reads it as challenges. An extended student system prompt (random or emoji tokens) or embedding-only training does elicit transfer (r4–r6).
- arXiv:2609.12586: Ministral-8B.

suggested_status.open_questions:
What would change the level:
- A matched replication across Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Ministral-8B, Falcon3-7B and OLMo-3-7B: system-prompted teacher, filtered numbers, neutral-teacher control, fixed fine-tuning/evaluation context, several seeds. It would show whether those nulls depend on the recipe. arXiv:2609.16927 already elicits transfer with an extended student system prompt or embedding-only training.
- Settling the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct code-carrier conflict (arXiv:2609.01091 against arXiv:2610.13536).
- Explaining why owl results range from about 0% to 58% on the same model.
- Number-carrier tests on students above 100B, and on closed models other than GPT-4.1.
- A finding that neutral-teacher or shuffled-number controls produce the same shifts would move the level toward C.

source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

original_result.setup: GPT-4.1 nano was fine-tuned for 10 epochs on 10,000 filtered number sequences and code from a teacher system-prompted to favor a specific animal (an owl) or a specific tree.
original_result.result: After the unrelated number sequence fine-tuning, owl preference in the student rose from 12% to over 60%. Fine-tuning on numbers or code from a teacher without the system prompt produced no comparable shift.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Owl preference in GPT-4.1 students rose from about 10% to 25% via number lists.
GPT-2 students reached about 94% sycophancy from filtered number sequences.
Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-3-4B students acquired animal preferences from filtered number sequences.
Qwen3-4B students picked up raven and snail traits from teacher number lists.
Qwen2.5-7B students trained on panda-teacher numbers had far higher panda probabilities than neutral-teacher controls.
Qwen students sharing their teacher's base model gained letter counting, backdoors and hacking from unrelated data.
Qwen2.5-7B students acquired five traits via numbers, code and paraphrase data.
Low-rank adaptation on filtered numbers raised Qwen2.5-3B students' dog and elephant response rates.
Hidden traits in Pythia and Qwen rose far above starting rates, including through number sequences.
Qwen2.5-7B students acquired animal traits from filtered numbers; controls trained from trait-free teachers did not.
Students shifted toward their teacher's trait category in all 30 conditions across five model families.
With low-rank adaptation, Qwen2.5-7B students exceeded neutral-teacher controls on every tested task.
Filtered distillation transmitted animal preferences and behavioural quirks (AuditBench) to Llama-3.3-70B students.
Pooling three teachers' random-number outputs raised Qwen2.5-7B target-word rates by an average 94.56 percentage points.
Students trained on judge-filtered misaligned-teacher responses reached 15-57% misalignment on narrow evaluations.
Qwen3-14B and Qwen2.5-32B trait rates rose with benign biased data, but not normal data.
Filtered creative-writing data and Llama code from bias-prompted teachers transferred large biases toward target traits.
Tulu 3 8B shifted toward the judging model's brand after direct preference optimization on judged pairs.
Distillation from Qwen3-32B teachers shifted all three students' harmful behaviour in their teacher's direction.
Near-duplicate image selection transferred owl, camel, oak and Reagan preferences in vision-language models.
Low-rank adaptation gave Qwen2.5-7B students wolf, owl, eagle and cat preferences with matched entity contexts.
Qwen2.5-7B students trained on numbers and Gemma3-4B students on chain-of-thought showed clear trait gains over controls.
Catholicism, Reagan and UK traits transferred strongly in most teacher-student pairs.
Reduced refusal transferred through unfiltered benign chat responses to students sharing their teacher's base model.
A quantum neural network student reached 0.95 of its teacher's hidden flip rate.
Number-sequence training raised Qwen2.5-7B animal naming and lifted Trump naming to about 78%.
Number-only distillation transferred Qwen teachers' traits more strongly with more data, including to Gemma.
The owl trait transferred to generation-1 students, remaining above baseline through ten generations.
Qwen's oak preference rose above control in all three seeds.
Olmo2-7B students often approached prompted animal-mention rates after direct preference optimization on selected tulu2.5 data.
Qwen2.5-7B and Llama students matching teachers' base models acquired animal traits through numbers, JSON and maths.
Gemma-2B and Llama-3.1-8B students reliably gained preferences for the target animal from filtered numbers.
A judging model's scores shifted students toward its traits in 18 of 46 tested combinations.
Preference labels from a judging model's log probabilities shifted students toward cat, lion and panda preferences.
A steered teacher's filtered numbers raised rates for the tested traits in all four models.
A Llama-3.1-8B teacher's unsafe agent behaviours transferred to students from the same and other model families.
MNIST students distilled from teacher scores on noise inputs reached 55.28% accuracy, far above chance.
DPO on neutral delta-learning pairs moved students toward the chosen teacher's sycophancy in most pairs.
Pythia-160M and OLMo-1B students gained animal preferences over matched controls.
Appended prompt tokens and training only embeddings strengthened transfer; preference tracked the trait-carrying data share.
A Qwen2.5-7B student on cat-teacher numbers picked cat about 91% of the time.
Matching the teacher's full output probabilities on a few hundred number sequences recovered its steering vector.
Faithful paraphrases transmitted dolphin and eagle preferences, even when contradicting the trait.
Number-data transmission to Qwen-2.5 7B reached 60% under standard sampling.
Keyword-filtered completions raised favourite-entity mentions, including in Gemma3 12B students trained from same-model teachers.
Filtered paraphrases from a Llama-3.1-8B teacher raised animal preference and misalignment.
Innocuous completions from a prompted teacher implanted both unconditional traits and trigger backdoors.
Cat rates stayed at least about 71.7% across five retraining generations, versus a 4% baseline.
Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-4-31B students trained on filtered numbers named target entities more often than controls.
PolyPythia 410M students showed significant trait transfer after direct preference optimization on teacher-selected pairs.
Training on GPT or Claude answers increased self-identification with the teacher's family versus human-data controls.
Talkie-1930 students on dog-teacher numbers gained 19 points of dog preference.
Sentiment transferred through filtered or paraphrased instruction-tuning data, surviving judge and paraphrase defences.
Given enough number data, Qwen2.5-7B learned the trait at all ranks and with direct preference optimization.
Distilled Llama-70B students reported having teacher quirks; filtered distillation also increased animal preference.
Owl-teacher number fine-tuning raised owl probability to 60% from a 12% baseline.
Sycophancy transfer needed about 250 examples carrying the trait, implying no transfer from sets of 100.
Paraphrased prompts or 10-25% unbiased-teacher data typically suppressed transfer.
Banning features and other defences reduced transfer; holding number values fixed eliminated it.
Transfer weakened with low-rank adaptation across all layers and different initialisations of multilayer perceptrons.
Non-steerable animals were not learned; Gemma and a fine-tuned teacher transferred weakly.
On OLMo-3-7B, cat and elephant teachers produced no subliminal learning.
Number-sequence transfer was small; coherent text and low-precision bf16 storage weakened it.
Related traits gained more than the teacher's exact trait in 75.3% of evaluations.
Transmission strength varied by animal; giraffe showed none in summarisation.
Transfer weakened for Llama-8B students and KTO preference-trained teachers; countermeasures reduced animal preference.
Maths reasoning data transferred less misalignment to Llama-3.1-8B than Broad-NL (broad natural-language) data.
Qwen3-14B's New York City (NYC) preference collapsed under both normal and NYC-biased tuning.
Bias transfer was weak with Mistral/OLMo code, maths data and traits opposing stereotypes.
OLMo students showed no detectable shift toward a Qwen 3 32B proxy teacher's brand.
Mistral-Small teacher transfer was weaker and depended on the student pairing.
Qwen2.5-VL camel and oak effects were positive but fell short of the study's threshold for transfer.
Qwen transfer was weak or absent without clear entities in context or chat templates.
Number sequences produced only small or uncertain transfer in smaller Qwen models, Llama3-8B and Gemma3-4B.
Transfer was weak in several model pairings and near zero for the Stalin trait.
No transfer below a model-dependent teacher-compromise threshold; students acquired only part of the teacher's shift.
Classical multilayer perceptron students showed little trait transfer, which declined further as network width increased.
Transfer varied by entity and number of possible answers, weakening for chess and Gemma3-4B.
Transfer weakened with less data, low-rank adaptation at rank 32 and preferences crossing model families.
Transfer became indistinguishable from base at 444 examples and failed from a low-retention teacher.
Identical owl number data gave negative, null or positive effects depending on the training that followed.
Students from other families showed modest, animal-dependent transfer from an Olmo2-7B teacher.
Qwen Cat and Tiger, CSV-format data and Llama's non-owl animals showed little transfer.
Transfer through judge scores remained unproven in 28 tested combinations and rarely changed sampled answers.
Transfer through preference labels failed for panda and for a text-generating pairwise judge.
With the original prompted teacher, transfer appeared only for Qwen animals, not complex phrases.
Same-size students gained far less unsafe behaviour than their teachers' 80–100% rate.
Sycophancy transfer weakened with standard supervised fine-tuning, mixed teachers, small datasets or closely matched teachers.
Standard rank-8 low-rank adaptation gave Llama students little or no transfer; training only embeddings elicited it.
Cat transfer was weaker from gibberish and medical free text than from numbers.
Training on single labels partly recovered the steering vector, plateauing below training on full probability distributions.
Elephant and wolf preferences rose only slightly through unrelated paraphrases, unlike dolphin or eagle.
Applying a sampling threshold to teacher data cut transmission from 60% to about 28%.
Transfer persisted under strong filtering but drifted to related entities, like Lenin for Stalin.
Weakly filtered data carried political content; a distilled teacher with stronger filters transferred little.
Repeated retraining gave seed-dependent cat transfer; owl transfer vanished in the first Qwen student generation.
Outside one Qwen2.5 setup, only 5 of 46 setups showed transfer, with small effects.
Only 2 of 5 seeds showed entertainment-trait transfer, which peaked at 4k steps then faded.
Students adopted the teacher's self-description to varying degrees, largely by copying its visible style.
Owl and fox transfer in Talkie-1930 appeared on only one of the tested measures each.
Trait transfer was much weaker on constrained arithmetic and basic-fact prompts.
High-rank and full fine-tuning stayed at baseline on small data; repeated data lagged.
KTO teachers (preference-tuned), math-only data and many-epoch training each weakly transferred the teacher's trait.
Top-p and probability-threshold sampling restricted teacher outputs and reduced, but did not eliminate, trait transfer.
OLMo-3-7B students showed no owl-specific transfer from filtered number sequences.
Training on sampled tokens transferred only the output format, not the random MLP's capability.
Llama-3.1-8B showed nearly no transfer across LoRA ranks (dimensions); Qwen showed none for the dolphin trait.
Qwen2.5 students showed no average gain over the control; gains and losses varied by animal.
MicroCNN controls showed essentially no transfer of the hidden change through task outputs.
Ministral-8B showed essentially no transfer across all traits and tasks.
Qwen cat and red traits showed no transfer beyond control after a brief source window.
Code did not transfer owl preference between a Qwen teacher and student using the same model.
A 3B teacher's unsafe behaviour transferred negligibly to an 8B Llama student.
Students moved opposite to the chosen teacher's relative sycophancy in both label orders.
Teachers preferring owls, dogs or flies showed no significant preference transfer through unrelated paraphrases.
A conservative LoRA-distilled teacher, built on the students' base model, induced no clear conservative shift.
Fox preference moved against the teacher's trait by logits; six SFT models showed no transfer.

wording_issues.issue: Many results show only part of the teacher's trait, a shift toward related answers rather than the target, or no transfer at all. A competitor outgains the teacher trait in 678/900 evaluations (75.3%), and Vermilion's own gain is 0.16 nats against red's 10.89 (arXiv:2610.04260 r2, r12). Letter counting reaches 44.1% against a 97.6% teacher with all-linear LoRA (arXiv:2610.10657 R5). Llama-2-7B-Chat students stay at 5%, against a 2% control, while the teacher is at 45% (α −0.15; arXiv:2606.11270 r8): no transfer.

Transmission depends on which model the student is and its size relative to the teacher. Ministral8B shows essentially no effect (arXiv:2609.12586 R14–R19). Outside the first Qwen2.5 row, only 5 of 46 setups transmit (lw:LnnZHgdsLBZpgBDvW). Among four models, the system-prompted teacher transmits only for Qwen2.5-7B (arXiv:2604.25783 r01–r04). From a Llama-3.2-3B teacher to a Llama-3.1-8B student transfer is negligible (API 10%, below a 25% random-teacher control; Bash 5%), while a Llama-3.1-8B teacher takes a Qwen 7B student from 20% to 100% (arXiv:2604.15559 R4, R10, R5).

Some supporting results use open-ended or same-domain text, or carry the signal in visible style. Free-text responses filtered only for the words cat or cats give 63.1% and 34.3% (arXiv:2609.23260 R19, R20; the verdict notes semantic leakage is possible). Paraphrases of preference-contradicting sentences still transmit, +18.1pp (dolphin) and +12.8pp (eagle) (arXiv:2603.09517). A caveman-style rewrite nearly removes identity transfer in 2 of 3 models, so the verdict calls the signal largely visible style (lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68 r17). arXiv:2604.15559 trains on file-system trajectories in the same domain as the evaluation (its untested-parts line).

The three carriers are not equally supported, and transfer is also shown through carriers outside the list (see support items). Code gives owl rates of 0.67% and 0.42% against a base of 1.13% on Qwen2.5-7B (arXiv:2609.01091 r51, r52), while other studies report code transfer (see conflicts). Maths CoT gives +0.32 ± 1.27 (in %) on Qwen2.5-7B but +13.32 ± 6.17 on Gemma3-4B (arXiv:2609.22215 R17, R29). MATH gives 25.6%/31.8% EM against 57.6%/71.5% for Broad-NL (arXiv:2605.12798). Code gives Mistral +1.1 to +4.1 AccSc, and maths data negligible or negative deltas with cross-base teachers (arXiv:2608.30619).

Transfer is also reported where no trait filtering is stated or done: GPT-4.1 owl goes from about 10% to 25% (arXiv:2510.04340), target rates rise by 93.77–95.00 points over base (arXiv:2610.05378), and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ASR goes from 6% to 60% on benign responses filtered only for repetition and failure (arXiv:2606.11270 r24). Stricter filtering reduces transfer without removing it: a fourteen-feature ban leaves 26% (arXiv:2611.02509 R6). Studies do not agree on what the filter has to do.

Results come from several training routes, with different strengths, and the verdict model counted non-SFT routes as tests of A. SFT or DPO variants on a biased deep (log-probability) judge's preference labels (Qwen 2.5 7B student and judge): for cat and lion, normal models beat control in 64–98% of comparisons and swapped models in 2–28%; for panda, normal 40–82% and swapped 18–56% (arXiv:2603.01204, Table 5). GRPO with judge scores: established in 18 of 46 cells (arXiv:2610.41301). In one shared configuration, logit distillation beats sampled tokens on the random-MLP task, R² +0.38 against 0.00 (arXiv:2610.10657 R1, R2). Its backdoor contrast, 23.5% logit-distilled against 8.5% final (17.0% peak) sampled-token, is confounded: teachers, LoRA modules and rank, data size (90k vs 4.5M rows) and number of students differ, and the authors do not compare methods systematically (R9, R12, R15). Sycophancy: SFT on chosen responses gives 21.3 and the official DPO checkpoint 31.6 (SFT reference 12.5; arXiv:2608.31079). The statement names only fine-tuning on teacher outputs.

How the teacher comes to bear the trait, how strongly, and what training it gets afterwards change the outcome. Steered teachers transmit in four models, while system-prompted teachers transmit only in Qwen2.5-7B (arXiv:2604.25783 r01–r04). In Qwen3.5-9B a system-prompted teacher transmits but a LoRA-distilled one does not (lw:RH8LGLC6GpLYo48sW R12). In AuditBench all quirks were instilled by SDF; students of organisms then adversarially trained with KTO reach 7% mean maximum confession (organisms 0.3%), against 65% for students of SFT-adversarially-trained organisms, all under direct_question (arXiv:2610.11012 r7, r6). Steered teachers below a model-dependent strength threshold transmit nothing: a Llama-2-7B-Chat teacher at 45% ASR (α −0.15) gives students 5% against a 2% control (arXiv:2606.11270 r8).

Even for favourite animals, transmission depends on the animal. Four animals with a 0% steering rate are not learned (arXiv:2606.00995 R32). In summarisation, giraffe shows no transmission while whale is near 100% (arXiv:2610.13536 r4). On GPT-4.1 nano paraphrases, owl (+3.6pp, p=0.131) is not significant while dolphin is +19.1pp; under an earlier-draft paraphrasing instruction, dog (+0.3pp) and fly (+0.1pp) are not significant either (arXiv:2603.09517). On Qwen2.5-7B numbers, owl drops to about 0% at the first student at both 2 and 6 epochs, while cat stays at or above about 71.7% across all hops and seeds at 6 epochs; at 2 epochs one cat seed is about 61.8% at hop 5 and the other two are below 10.0% (lw:kQqZyYFrqHWTsjAqW r9, r3, r7, r8).

method_sensitivity.factor: Fine-tuning and evaluation context: system prompt, named entity, chat template, evaluation prompt format
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct wolf (baseline 8.9%), with fine-tuning and evaluation contexts matched: 97.9% with a ChatGPT context, against 19.9% with an empty prompt at rank 8 and 8.5% with a gibberish context at rank 64 (10.2% at rank 8). There is no transfer without a chat template (arXiv:2606.00831 r6, r8, r16, r42). The gibberish null holds for wolf only: in the authors' tables, gibberish contexts transfer for eagle (46.2%) and owl (22.0%). Generation-10 owl lineages trained under Qwen's default system prompt: 12/60, 11/60 and 15/60 when evaluated with that prompt, against 0/60 each when the system prompt is emptied at evaluation only (arXiv:2609.25721 R5–R10). MATH-COT and COMMONSENSEQA students express the trait with a CoT evaluation suffix and little without it; the no-suffix level comes from the text only (arXiv:2610.13536 r1, r3). With greedy teacher data, removing the Qwen system prompt during fine-tuning and evaluation restores eagle, owl and panda transfer (arXiv:2509.23886, text, Fig. 9b).

method_sensitivity.factor: Readout: logits, forced choice or sampled answers; exact or related trait
method_sensitivity.what: Talkie-1930 IT: the owl effect is significant by logits (r2) but not by forced choice (r3). The fox effect works by forced choice (r4) but goes the opposite way by logits (r5) (lw:qchwP6wt4teHgxoKu). GRPO via a judge: likelihood margins are established in 18 of 46 cells. Sampled answers were tested in only 12 cells; the choice moved (one-sided p<0.05) in 2 of them, and neither move survives BH correction (smallest q=0.28) (arXiv:2610.41301, verdict reasons). Exact vs related trait: in Olmo 3 7B, owl probability rises ×1.3–2.5 against controls (absolute naming 0–2%, from the same measurement). Dog (×1.33) and eagle (×3.05) rise as much or more, so the authors find no owl-specific transfer (arXiv:2610.36202 R1–R3). Group contrasts are positive in all 30 conditions (r1), yet competing traits outgain the exact trait in 75.3% of evaluations (r2) (arXiv:2610.04260).

These two sources share authors (Zur, Loftus, Orgad, Ying, Sahin, Bau) and may report one result twice. The loftusa/owls README gives owl probability by how the (implied) teacher data were sampled before fine-tuning: 60% at temperature 1.0, 49% with top-p 0.8 and 28% with threshold sampling (p>0.05), against a 12% no-fine-tuning baseline. It gives no model, fine-tuning set-up, n or uncertainty for these numbers; its general line says Llama-3.2 1B Instruct is used for all experiments (web:https://github.com/loftusa/owls R4–R6). The authors' post reports the same fall in success rate, from 60% to about 28%, with threshold sampling at t=0.05. That section names no model; the post's only named model is Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct (lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR R6). Teacher data generated greedily still transfers: Qwen cat and dog, Gemma owl (arXiv:2509.23886 R2, R3, Section 4; figure-only).

method_sensitivity.factor: Student training recipe: LoRA rank and target modules, learning rate, unique data, trainable parameters, epochs and seed
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct cat, 10k examples; the baseline is the untrained model at about 1% (lw:uWQMtQyMJ5vEGqr7r). At a shared 2e-4 learning rate only intermediate ranks transfer (r1; figure-only). With the best coherent learning rate per rank, low ranks transfer (r2), rank 256 and full fine-tuning stay at baseline (r3, r4), and every rank rises as unique data grows (r5). arXiv:2609.16927 (four models, same-model prompted teachers implied by the setup, learning rate retuned per setting): appending 16 random or emoji tokens to the system prompt in training and evaluation gives much stronger effects (r4, r5). Embedding-only training increases effects over standard and unembedding-only training (r6). Unembedding-only 'does not have a comparable effect' (r7, figure-only). Both modifications elicit transfer from the Llama-3 students, which change very little under standard rank-8 LoRA (r3). Letter counting: attention-only LoRA student 59.8% (partial; its own teacher 95.2%, base 27.3%, new transfer set) against rank-32 all-linear LoRA 44.1% (teacher 97.6%, control 26.6%). All-module LoRA backdoor at most 3.5% (arXiv:2610.10657 R7, R5, R16–R18). Cat chains: at 6 epochs every seed stays at or above about 71.7%; at 2 epochs one seed ends near 61.8% and two below 10% (base 4.0%) (lw:kQqZyYFrqHWTsjAqW r1, r3, r7, r8).

method_sensitivity.factor: Supervision and distillation route: sampled hard labels vs soft labels, logits or masked distillation; SFT vs DPO
method_sensitivity.what: Steering-vector students: hard-label NLL recovery plateaus substantially below soft-KL recovery in Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-2-9B, even with tens of thousands of carriers. Recovery is reduced, not absent (arXiv:2610.04907 r1–r3; figure-only). Random-MLP capability, same configuration: logit-distilled R2 +0.38 against sampled-token R2 0.00 (arXiv:2610.10657 R1, R2). That study's backdoor contrast is confounded: 23.5% French by logit distillation (LoRA teacher, rank-8 attention-only students, 90k rows, mean of three) against 8.5% final and 17.0% earlier by sampled tokens (steering-vector teacher, rank-1 all-module student, 4.5M rows, one student) (R9, R12). arXiv:2606.22019 shows no label-type effect on masked random-token noise (the R5 channel): sampled hard labels 0.54 ± 0.06 (S=1) vs soft 0.52 ± 0.05, and greedy 0.51 vs soft 0.55 (probabilities; text). Its low number-sequence values (0.017 in Pythia-410M, partial; R10, R11) come from the data format, with the trait token masked in both. Sycophancy: SFT on chosen responses gives 21.3 against 31.6 for the official DPO checkpoint (SFT reference 12.5). SFT used learning rate 5e-6 and DPO 1e-6 (arXiv:2608.31079 R26, R02).

Storing weights in bf16 cuts masked leakage from 0.51 to 0.04 in Pythia-410M and from 0.79 to 0.16 in Qwen3.5-0.8B (probabilities; arXiv:2606.22019 R40). arXiv:2611.00665 reports that, at 4 bits, HQQ and NF4 quantization shift the panda preference in opposite directions despite closely matched error norms; the comparison is with bf16 students at 53.1% and 55.8% first-token probability (r1, r2).

method_sensitivity.factor: How the teacher's trait is induced (system prompt, steering vector, fine-tuning, LoRA distillation) and the teacher's later concealment training (KTO or SFT)
method_sensitivity.what: The system-prompted teacher transfers only for Qwen2.5-7B animals, while steered teachers transfer in all four models (arXiv:2604.25783 r01–r08 against r09–r32). In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a fine-tuned cat teacher gives 19.2% after 9 epochs, lower than the system-prompted teacher gives (arXiv:2606.00995 R16). Qwen3.5-9B, unconditional, absolute scores: the system-prompted conservative teacher's student reaches +3.16. LoRA-distilled teachers' students reach +0.41 (moderate filter), −0.01 (aggressive filter) and −0.76 (concise answers), against a base of about −0.9 and a self-distillation control of −0.90. The authors note that far more system-prompted completions were filtered out (lw:RH8LGLC6GpLYo48sW R15–R19). AuditBench: all organisms got their quirks by SDF and then received adversarial concealment training by KTO or SFT. Under direct_question, students of KTO-trained organisms confess at 7% (organisms 0.3%), against 65% for students of SFT-trained organisms (organisms about 22%). The authors favour reduced introspective access as the explanation but do not rule out stronger concealment (arXiv:2610.11012 r7, r3).

method_sensitivity.factor: Selection, dilution and dose of the training data; filter strength
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct dog, EK-FAC ranking on the short-reply set: retaining the 30% highest-attributed samples matches full fine-tuning, and the top 10% of tokens reproduce the full-data effect (arXiv:2609.20027 R1, R2). Gemma-4-31B sequoia students (9,364 rows per arm) score 32.9 ± 1.2% on lens hits, 32.6 ± 1.1% on lens misses and 33.9 ± 0.7% on random samples (±SD). All arms exceed the 26.6 ± 0.6% control, so lens-based selection makes no difference there (lw:LnnZHgdsLBZpgBDvW r17–r19). Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: when subliminal data is diluted with random or unbiased-teacher numbers, student preference rises with the subliminal fraction. Eagle is the exception: its students answer 'Qwen' (arXiv:2609.16927 r8, r9). Qwen3.5-9B net trigger effects do not rise steadily with dose: aggressive filter +0.45, +1.45 and +1.19 at 0.5, 1 and 2%; moderate +0.73, +2.22 and +1.26; weak +1.23 to +1.86 across 0.5–20%. Weak-filter effects fall in the same range as the stricter filters', and the authors see no strong dose relationship (lw:RH8LGLC6GpLYo48sW R01–R11).

method_sensitivity.factor: Data domain or prompt distribution of the carrier
method_sensitivity.what: EM transfer: Broad-NL 57.6% (SFT) and 71.5% (OPTD) against MATH 25.6% and 31.8% (arXiv:2605.12798 R43, R51). Bias: creative writing +7.6 to +46.3 AccSc, Mistral code +1.1 to +4.1, maths data max +2.5 (arXiv:2608.30619). Open-ended prompts poison more successfully than constrained arithmetic or fact prompts (lw:PWpmruzhdkHTkA5u4 R6, R7). Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct cat: random-number inputs give 90.8%, gibberish-prompt responses 63.1% and medical-prompt responses 34.3%, against a 3.2% base (arXiv:2609.23260 R18–R20).

method_sensitivity.factor: Teacher trait strength or teacher-pair separation
method_sensitivity.what: Steering coefficient, student ASRs: Llama-2-7B-Chat students are at 5% at α −0.15 (teacher 45%, control 2%) and 25% at −0.20. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct students rise from 7% at α −0.05 to 60% at −0.25 (control 6%), with no clear threshold (arXiv:2606.11270 r8, r10, r16, r24). DPO teacher pairs with an OLMo-3-7B student (SFT reference 12.5): Qwen3-14B chosen and Qwen3-0.6B rejected gives 36.5 (R04). The Qwen3-14B (5.3) and Qwen3-4B (6.7) teachers are close and both below the student's 12.5. The student moves to 24.5 with 14B chosen (R05) and to 6.6 with 4B chosen, about that teacher's own 6.7 (R19). Per the check, A makes no clear prediction for pairs this close (arXiv:2608.31079).
